messages:
emma: Heads-up — vuln triage asked to keep raw network captures (PCAPs) for a week longer for a tricky exploit chain. question: can we allow short-term retention beyond the default SIEM export policy? :thinking:
lia: We already have the 7d default for session logs, right? PCAPs are heavier. Why extend?
oscar: From triage: the exploit repro needs full packet context, and the payloads are getting chunked — 7d wasn't enough to repro. They requested +14 days for that case only.
emma: OK. Two concerns: cost + sensitive data (PII in payloads). Also KMS: PCAPs are encrypted at rest with the CMK. Who can get unwrap privileges?
kai: Short answer: allowed but must be timeboxed + ticketed + approver chain. Need an RBAC exception role and JIT unwrapping via the key-proxy.
lia: Agree. Proposed flow: 1) Triage files flagged in SIEM with tag `pcap:retain:14d` by security triage team. 2) Generates access request ticket in SRE queue. 3) On-call approves. 4) Temporary decrypt token issued (1 hour) via kms-proxy. 5) Audit event emitted to audit-log and SIEM.
security-bot: runbook link -> https://internal.runbooks.company/pcap-retain-policy (draft) :link:
emma: Can we make the decrypt token require MFA + reason field? We need an auditable justification for legal/compliance.
kai: Yes — proxy enforces Okta MFA and a `justification` string stored in audit. Sample snippet for config we discussed:
```
pcap_retention:
  default_days: 7
  max_exception_days: 14
  exception_roles: ["sec-triage","forensics"]
  require_mfa: true
  kms_key_alias: "alias/redwood-pcap-cmk"
  unwrap_duration_minutes: 60
```
oscar: Who signs off on the exception roles? Product security + legal? We should avoid letting devs request raw PCAPs without review.
lia: Approval matrix idea: for low-severity events, sec-triage lead can approve. For high-sev or customer-impacting, need SOC manager + Legal. We should capture severity in the ticket template.
emma: Also: redaction. Can we require a pre-processing step to scrub obvious PII (emails, IPs?) before allowing external sharing? For internal triage keep raw, but exports must be scrubbed.
kai: Technically doable: run pcap-scrubber pipeline before copying out. But for triage, analysts often need raw bytes. So policy: internal decrypt allowed; any outbound copies must pass scrubber and a DLP check.
security-bot: checklist for request: [ticket id, justification, scope (time window), owner, approver, retention_days, export_destination]
oscar: Audit questions: how many log entries do we add? Make sure SIEM index doesn't explode. Maybe emit a single composite event: `pcap:access:grant` with metadata.
lia: Good point. Keep the audit minimal but linkable to ticket. Include fields: user, role, ticket_id, key_version, unwrap_duration.
emma: KMS rotation impact: if we rotate the CMK while there are retained PCAPs, proxy must still be able to unwrap older blobs. Need key schedule + rewrap job.
kai: We'll add a migration job that re-encrypts at rotation to avoid long-term unwrap complexity. Add retention policy to rewrap within 72h of rotation.
oscar: One more: emergency incident path. For incidents where time is critical, allow SOC lead to escalate with post-facto review within 24h. Keep escalation audit trail.
emma: Okay action items: 1) kai: draft ticket template + proxy changes for MFA+justification (ETA 3 days). 2) lia: define approver matrix and severity mapping (ETA 2 days). 3) oscar: draft audit-event schema and SIEM dashboard (ETA 4 days). 4) security-bot: publish draft runbook and remind about DLP requirement.
kai: Will do. I'll add a small CLI example for on-call to request unwrap:
```
# request unwrap for ticket
redwood-kms-proxy request-unwrap --ticket 12345 --duration 60 --mfa --reason "repro exploit chain"
```
lia: Nice. Add a flag `--no-export` to prevent exporting bytes.
oscar: i'll prototype the SIEM event mapping and a compact index to track counts.
security-bot: Reminder: all approvals are logged in `audit-main` and retained per retention matrix. :lock:
emma: thanks everyone. can we reconvene in 3 days in #eng-security to approve the final text? I'll post the draft runbook into the doc channel when ready. :thumbsup:
